title: Traffic Shield: Incremental Exposure & Fallbacks for Pinned Model Promotion
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a staged promotion pattern (Traffic Shield) for upgrading pinned model revisions that combines incremental traffic exposure, synchronous shadow validation, and an automated fallback/quorum rollback mechanism. Goal is to let teams promote new model versions behind pins with low blast radius while surfacing multi-signal regressions (latency, token-cost delta, semantic regressions) before a full promotion.
background: We currently allow pinning a model revision and manual traffic switches, but large upgrades require manual monitoring and ad-hoc rollbacks. Recent internal incidents show latent semantic regressions passed surface tests but produced degraded outputs in edge cohorts. This ticket defines a reproducible baked-in promotion flow for pinned revisions with clear guardrails and telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Console: option to create a 'Traffic Shield' promotion when editing a pin that defines start_percentage, ramp_steps, cohort_rules, and auto-rollback thresholds
Runtime: ability to route X% of user traffic to candidate revision while synchronously shadowing requests to candidate for enriched comparison without charging production quota for shadowed path
Telemetry: multi-signal regression check implemented with configurable weights (latency, cost_delta, correctness_score) and a single composite regression_score exposed in dashboard
Safety: auto-rollback triggers if composite regression_score exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive evaluation windows or if latency SLO is breached by candidate beyond configured margin
Docs: new docs and runbook published with examples, failure modes, and playbook for manual override
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Design (1 week): finalize UX and policy knobs; align on signals and default thresholds
Phase 1 - Runtime + Router (2 sprints): add percentage-split routing behind pin, synchronous shadowing hook, token-cost accounting for shadow runs
Phase 2 - Telemetry (1 sprint): dashboarding, composite regression_score calculation, cohort-based breakdowns
Phase 3 - Console UX & Rollout APIs (1 sprint): UI for Traffic Shield creation, history of promotions, manual override, and audit logs
Phase 4 - Pilot (2 weeks): run with 3 internal teams, iterate thresholds and default knobs
Phase 5 - GA: enable by default for pinned promotions with opt-out and communicate to customers
telemetry_signals: p95_request_latency_ms: breakouts by route and user_cohort
semantic_regression_score: BLEU/ROUGE-style proxy + embedding cosine drift against control outputs
quality_health_index: weighted composite exposed to UI
fallback_playbook: Immediate rollback: if auto-rollback fires, route 100% back to last-good revision and mark promotion as failed
Quorum rollback: require 3 consecutive windows of threshold breach before auto-rollback unless latency SLO exceeded by >50% then immediate revert
Partial rollback: pin-level override to cap candidate traffic to 0% to preserve metrics for debugging
Incident workflow: open an incident with prepopulated tags (pin, candidate_revision, baseline_revision, cohorts) and attach last 100 sampled requests
Post-mortem: attach regression_score decomposition to postmortem and proposed mitigations
ux_considerations: Default thresholds should be conservative: composite_regression_threshold=0.15, latency_margin=1.2x p95
Expose an 'explain' panel in the Console showing top contributing signals to regression_score
Enable customers to create custom cohort filters (by route, user_token_prefix, enterprise_id) for targeted promotions
Audit log must show who created promotion, start/end times, and who triggered manual rollback
